audit.whatIsWrong: Chart hands Lillia level 1 and level 6 and calls level 2 even, then gives Fiora the 2-item stage — every one of those is contradicted by the page's own text.
audit.why: whys[0] calls her 'one of the weakest early laners' against an elite level 1; whys[1] says she cannot peel you; whys[4] says Grand Challenge clinches the all-in at 6; whys[6] and late say the 2-item stage slips toward her. packet.levelChart is Fiora x6 then Skill.
audit.corrected: win[0], win[1], win[4] and phases[0], phases[1], phases[4] -> Fiora; win[6]/phases[6] -> Skill, ratings rebalanced.

audit.whatIsWrong: The tracked spell is listed as Blooming Blows — her 6s basic damage/move-speed ability — when the spell that actually decides a commit is Lilting Lullaby. No cooldowns given anywhere.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 and comes back faster than any trade; Lilting Lullaby is 150/130/110 and is her only reset. Swirlseed is a flat 12s. Fiora W is 24s, R 110s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2] and dontsFull[0].d now point at Lilting Lullaby with 150s, and carry 12s Swirlseed, 6s Blooming Blows, 24s Riposte and 110s Grand Challenge.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] told you to Riposte Blooming Blows. That ability is a self-centred damage burst on a 6s cooldown — parrying it burns a 24s W on her cheapest spell; the parry target is her R.
audit.why: Riot's text: Blooming Blows damages nearby enemies and stacks her move speed; Lilting Lullaby is the drowsy-into-sleep that is the only thing capable of cancelling your engage.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].t/.d retargeted to Lilting Lullaby; dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d now say why parrying her Q is the losing trade. Also note Swirlseed keeps rolling until it hits a wall or target — it can come back at you off terrain from off-screen.

edits.before: - Lillia Blooming Blows: matchup-defining — Her kite + move speed stacks. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Lillia Lilting Lullaby: matchup-defining — 150s at rank 1, her only answer to your all-in. - Swirlseed: 12s at every rank. - Riposte: 24s, saved for her R. - Grand Challenge: 110s.

edits.before: Her kite + move speed stacks. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Her kite and move-speed stacks. Swirlseed is 12s — walk in on it.

edits.before: Q-lunge the exposed vital on Lillia, AA once, and E-slow out — repeat until his bar forces the all-in he loses.
edits.after: Q-lunge the exposed vital on Lillia, AA once, E-slow out — Vital procs cut your Q toward its 6s floor.

edits.before: Lillia wastes Blooming Blows — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Lillia spends R — 150s at rank 1. Commit the full pattern now.

edits.before: That is Lillia's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Blooming Blows is 6s at rank 1 — parrying it wastes W on her cheapest spell.

edits.before: Burning Riposte on poke — your W exists to delete his ONE key spell; waste it and the duel maths flips against you.
edits.after: Riposte is 24s and it exists for Lilting Lullaby — spend it on DOT ticks and the sleep lands unanswered.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Grand Challenge's' in mid — FALSE POSITIVE, that is Fiora's own R. UNVERIFIED: four fields (whys[4], spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1]) claim Riposte parries Lilting Lullaby's drowsy/sleep into a return STUN. Riot's text says Riposte stuns only if it blocked an immobilizing effect and does not say whether drowsy (a slow) or the sleep itself qualifies, and the kits carry no eligibility data. I left that text untouched rather than assert either way. Many full-layer strings still call Lillia 'he/his'.
